prompt: Three small thin paper prints arriving on the open sea, carried by the current towards the viewer, floating on the water as lightly as a fallen leaf, seen from slightly above at a low angle, in perspective, so that each print appears as a foreshortened slanted quadrilateral lying on the water surface, never facing the viewer, never upright, never flat like a sticker. Each one is a single sheet of thin printing paper, paper-thin and weightless, with no visible thickness at its edges: one corner slightly lifted and curling upwards, the sheet bending gently to follow the swell, and one edge wet, slightly darker and translucent where it touches the water. Thin flexible paper only, never thick, never a slab, never a board, never a block. The three prints are small and far away, surrounded by a lot of open water: they come one after another from the far upper right towards the centre-right of the image, far apart, never touching, never overlapping, the farthest one tiny in the upper right, the middle one a little larger, the nearest one the largest but still small, only about one fifth of the image width, at the centre-right. Each print is turned at its own angle. Each print is a landscape sheet, about 3:2, wider than tall: an off-white #fbfcfd paper margin and, inside it, one large empty panel bounded by a thin crisp ink grey line. The panel is completely blank, one plain uniform flat light off-white tone, nothing drawn inside it, no picture, no pattern, no hatching, no shading, and it stays fully visible and dry, the water only touching the outer edge of the margin. One small saturated violet #7C5CD6 paper clip is clipped on the margin of the nearest print; it is the only violet in the whole image, and the paper margins of all three prints are plain off-white. The prints are drawn in crisp off-white and ink grey line art, their edges a single fine ink line. The water reacts to every print: a thin off-white foam line where the paper meets the water, small engraved ripples spreading from its edges, a short narrow wake of fine curved lines trailing behind it, pointing back towards the upper right where it came from, and a soft darker reflection drawn in denser line hatching just below it. Long gentle current lines flow across the sea from the upper right towards the centre-right, bringing the prints closer. Richly detailed engraved nautical chart style, like a fine antique sea chart printed in two inks: the sea built from many layers of fine wave lines and hatching, line density increasing towards the deep water to give depth, tonal bands from deep cerulean at the bottom to lighter cerulean at the top, bathymetric contour lines with small depth soundings drawn as tiny dots, subtle foam strokes and a few glints of light on the crests. Every wave is drawn as visible engraved line work, like a steel engraving, never painted, never smooth. Crisp sharp lines of several weights, intricate but calm, premium print quality, high detail, elegant. No photographic rendering, no glow, no gradient, no text, no letters, no numbers, no watermark, water filling the whole image edge to edge, the prints in the upper two thirds from the centre to the right, open calm water on the left third and along the bottom. Palette strictly limited to medium cerulean ocean blue #0072a8 and its tints and shades, off-white #fbfcfd, ink grey #13212b and saturated violet #7C5CD6 on the paper clip only.
